newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel breaks 3.34 to the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel breaks 3.34 to the dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell sharply against the dollar on Wednesday after the U.S. currency reached a 34-month high against the mark, dealers said.

"The dollar is very strong and its rise overseas was the main reason for the shekel's decline. The Bank of Israel continued buying dollars to support the basket and the business sector continued selling," said Zahi Elias at Bank Leumi.
The dollar rose as high as 3.3440 shekels but the shekel recovered slightly after the dollar slipped from its peak.
Traders estimated that the central bank bought almost $90 million in foreign currency to support the basket rate, which has been persistently trading at the bottom of its trading band.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3420 shekels against 3.3310 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6337 shekels against 3.6331 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6940 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7164 on Tuesday and against the mark at 1.9819 shekels against 1.9946 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3390 shekels.
